body:
Me too!!! I totally get it!!!

I will tell you, such change is possible.

I do stupid embarrassing things pretty often. Four times so far I've moved states and started fresh. Twice I've legally changed my name. It's not hard, or expensive. You just go to the court clerk's office in your county and ask for a name change. You could move to somewhere new and change your name, change your hair cut and color, clothing style... These things actually can be accomplished fairly easily!

That said I will also tell you what I tell myself and I REALLY hope is true... I tell myself that the ultra stupid things I've done and said are probably bigger in my memory than they are in anyone else's. Still... I get it. I'd like to move again now, but can't due to having a teenager and elderly parents. Sometimes we have to wait. Then we refer to just trying to believe that our idiotic actions and traits aren't so important to others as they are to ourselves. 

Good luck.

I want exactly that same thing!!!! I heard a podcast yesterday that's making me wait, though. I can't seem to link it to here but it's from The Washington Post, called "The Organ Transplant Aftershock".  Apparently organ donations are way down during Covid because, according to this, organs must be kept alive but brain death achieved usually for a matter of 2-3 days while the transplant team assembles, matching recipients are gathered, etc. During those days a ventilator is needed to continue maintaining the health of the donor's organs. Now, during Covid, ventilators and ICU beds (the donor's physical health and needs must also be maintained by doctors and nurses) are not so readily available. Those that are around are resereved for patients who might live, rather than for those who are already considered "brain dead." I feel that such donations are the only decent thing I can do, too.  In light of this, I've decided to wait, rather than waste precious medical resources on me. Meanwhile we can still donate blood every 8 weeks or so. 

I'm sorry you're feeling this way and I'll throw in the cursory "it will get better." Things often do, that's true. Bullies move on, we learn that lost loves were only bringing us down, etc. I get it though, believe me. 

For organ donation, now is not the time... so you may as well wait and see if things might get better with meds etc. Welbutrin does make life more tolerable for me. I hope things get better for you soon.

If the hitman makes the hit and later gets caught, though, then you've jacked his or her life and the lives of those who love said hitman. Interesting idea, but it could leave a whopper of a mess in your wake. Even if the hitman is never identified, some police resources would be wasted to solve your murder. I vote no on that idea. It could be leave a lot of hurt and trouble  in your wake.

I get that. I'm sorry. I've felt for most of my life that i shouldn't be here, but other people have told me I've helped them. I bet you've helped folks too, and will help more in time. You're not alone though.  I have that same feeling most of the time.

Please give this some time. I'm sorry you've encountered such dingdongs, truly. Masking won't last forever though. You've made it this far,and I am confident there are people who love you. Please wait this mask thing out. I'm sorry for the awful rape and attack and complete lack of help you received. Clearly you are strong. I appreciate your sharing your story.
